newsitem.title: UK: NatWest shares firm on fresh merger talk.
newsitem.headline: NatWest shares firm on fresh merger talk.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc rose on Monday after weekend press reports said the bank's major institutional investors were pressuring for a bid or merger.
The shares were up 9-1/2p at 790p by 0735 GMT.

The Sunday Times newspaper said six of NatWest's biggest institutional shareholders privately expresssed concern at the bank's share price performance. It said a break-up deal could value the underperforming stock at 10.00 stg.
One industry analyst, who declined to be named, said the 10.00 stg per share estimate of the banking group's break-up value seemed realistic.
"NatWest are undervalued fundamentally because of their management problems," the analyst said. "They are an under-utilised franchise."
The latest rumours followed reports last week that NatWest had approached Abbey National about creating a financial services giant but Abbey was said to have rejected the idea.
"There is no doubt that people are unhappy with NatWest," said the analyst. "They are desperate to get something done because they are not achieving the shareholder returns they said they would."
Analysts speculated that banking giant HSBC Holdings may consider making a bid for NatWest.

"NatWest's management has a poor reputation but the group has a good franchise," one said." By merging, the NatWest board would still have some sort of control over its future, but if they get taken over they won't."
